threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You'll know they're new when they ask for directions to the nearest Starbucks and blank at the sight of the independent coffee shops on every corner.
On the N87 last night, a guy serenaded a sleeping woman with a ukulele – she never even stirred. Clapham bus journeys are a performance art.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a group of kids playing footy in the street, dodging a passing bus and laughing. Just another Neukölln afternoon.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night kebab joint that serves currywurst with peanut sauce. It's like a culinary love child of two cities.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know which taquería secretly has the best late-night burritos, even if it looks closed.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tux on the 19 bus fiddling with a saxophone. Turns out he was headed to a wedding, almost missed his stop chatting with the driver.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think the Plaça del Sol is just a pretty square; locals know it’s a vibrant hub where the evening air buzzes with music and laughter.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a newbie by their reluctance to try a vermut before noon. It’s like they’re saving it for a special occasion.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground'—real locals know that’s where the good coffee shops are.
Caught a night bus last weekend—two guys argued over who could name the most obscure south London pubs. Turns out, one was a former bouncer from The Blue Anchor.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh döner mingling with the sound of a street musician playing an accordion at Hermannplatz—classic Neukölln moment.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a spontaneous techno party under an old railway bridge on a Tuesday night. Just bring your own drinks!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they still complain about BART even when the colors are fading. It's like the echo of frustration hangs in the air.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the bus stop with a saxophone while waiting for the 5. Only in SF do you get a live concert while you’re late to work.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think our quiet squares are just for sipping coffee; locals know they’re for late-night impromptu concerts under the stars.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they still hold onto their map, squinting at street names instead of using Google Maps.
